name: Protector-Incidence Transport Alphabet for Two-Repair Lifts
statement: In any trace-carrier scheme on an ample two-repair lift, the complete precedence alphabet is read from signed trace transport. An old-support carrier takes same-trace predecessors and protector choices from the union of the corresponding fibres in both sections. If a carrier on $D\cup\{e\}$ lies in layer $i$, all same-trace predecessors lie in layer $i$, while every trace on $D$ creates a protector demand in the corresponding opposite-layer fibre. Every directed trace circuit is therefore a finite word in old-support, same-layer, and cross-layer incidence types, and its number of cross-layer arcs is even.
proof: Carrier precedence and protector arcs depend only on membership in the relevant trace fibres. The old-support transport formula expresses each fibre as the union of its two section fibres. The vertical transport formula confines same-trace predecessors to the carrier's layer and identifies every opposite-layer protector fibre. These give the listed incidence types. Traversing a closed directed walk must return to its initial layer, so layer changes occur an even number of times.
comments: This is a transport law for any chosen trace-carrier scheme. It does not assert acyclicity or the existence of a globally compatible carrier choice.
